Student Clubs and Organizations
Our clubs and organizations bring students together around shared interests, leadership, service, culture, and recreation. Whether you want to join an existing group or explore something new, there’s a place for you.
Get Involved on Campus
Student involvement is a core part of the Cal State Monterey Bay experience. Clubs and organizations provide opportunities to build community, develop leadership skills and engage with campus life in meaningful ways.
We support student organizations through dedicated councils that offer guidance, resources and leadership development. Each council focuses on a different type of involvement, helping students find the right fit for their interests and goals.
Whether you are interested in academics, culture, recreation, service or leadership, there is a place to get involved.
Why Should You Join a Club?
Joining a student organization enhances your experience beyond academics. Those involved in clubs and organizations often develop skills that support personal growth, leadership and future success.
You’ll gain opportunities to:
Build leadership and teamwork skills
Connect with peers who share similar interests
Contribute to campus and community initiatives
Balance academics with involvement and service
Additionally, recognized student organizations receive access to campus support to help their group operate and grow, including:
Reserving classrooms, conference rooms and other campus spaces
Funding options for events and activities
Guidance and resources from student life staff
MyRaft
MyRaft
is CSUMB’s student engagement platform. Students use MyRaft to discover and join clubs and organizations, register for events, connect with campus resources and services, and interact with other students through posts and chat.
Student Organization Councils
Inter-Club Council (ICC)
Supports academic, cultural, identity-based, advocacy, faith and interest-based clubs. ICC helps organizations foster leadership development, campus engagement and collaboration across student groups.
Sports Club Council (SCC)
Supports student-led sports clubs focused on recreation, competition and wellness. SCC assists with organization oversight, risk management and leadership development for sports teams.
Greek Life Council (USFC)
Supports recognized fraternities and sororities at CSUMB. Greek Life organizations emphasize leadership, scholarship, service and community connection.
Frequently Asked Questions
Do I need prior experience to join a club or organization?
Unless otherwise stated, no experience is required. Most clubs welcome students who are new and curious, making them a great way to try something new. If you don’t see a club that fits your interests, starting one is easy—students can form a new club twice a year.
Can I join more than one organization?
Yes. Many students choose to participate in more than one club or organization, especially if their interests span different areas. We encourage you to explore what works best for you while being mindful of your time and commitments so you can stay balanced and focused on your academics.
Are clubs open to all majors?

Are clubs open to all majors?
Yes. All recognized clubs and organizations at CSUMB are open to students from all majors, with the exception of fraternities and sororities and honor societies. Clubs bring together students with diverse academic backgrounds, creating opportunities for collaboration, new perspectives and community. When choosing how to get involved, consider activities that fit your interests, academic goals and schedule.
How do I join or follow a club?
Most clubs and organizations use
MyRaft
to manage membership, share updates and promote events. Logging into MyRaft is the best way to explore opportunities and stay connected.

Mission
The mission of CAUSA is to raise awareness and create a supportive community for Central American students on campus. We strive to empower our members by sharing our unique cultural heritage and life stories, fostering a strong sense of identity in higher education. Through advocacy, cultural events, and educational initiatives, we aim to amplify the voices of Central Americans, challenge stereotypes, and promote inclusion and representation within the academic community. Our commitment is to provide a safe and welcoming space for all, where every member can grow, connect, and thrive while celebrating the richness of our Central American roots.
Membership Benefits
As a member of CAUSA, you will be part of a supportive and inclusive community that celebrates Central American heritage, fostering a sense of pride and identity within the campus. You’ll have the opportunity to develop leadership skills through active participation in club initiatives and advocacy efforts while building connections with students, faculty, and professionals who share an interest in Central American culture. Membership offers professional development opportunities, including experience in event planning, project management, and public speaking. You'll also participate in cultural events, workshops, and social gatherings that highlight and celebrate Central American traditions. Additionally, CAUSA provides a safe space to express yourself freely, discuss challenges unique to the Central American community, and be part of a movement advocating for representation and inclusion in higher education.

Mission
Our mission is to provide a space for Jews on campus to be their authentically Jewish selves and to uplift Jewish voices. We make it possible for Jewish students to stay connected with their Judaism while pursuing higher education. Whether it be for religious Jewish students who want a place to celebrate holidays, or for Jewish students who want to connect with their culture and community.
We will do this through weekly Shabbat gatherings on Friday evenings, holiday celebrations, and exploring and learning about Jewish culture. We can also have discussions where students will get the opportunity to talk about their experiences being Jewish and learn more about Jewish culture.

The benefits of membership are that Jewish students will get to have a community and a support system on campus. Jewish and non-Jewish students are welcome to come connect with each other and cultivate new friendships with people from different backgrounds. We also plan to have guest speakers come to club meetings, in person or over zoom.
Jewish students would have opportunities to learn more about their culture and history. They will be able to connect with their Judaism through shabbat dinners, events to celebrate our holidays, and potential field trips to the temple in Carmel. Weekly shabbat meetings would be a great time for students to relax and have conversations regarding Jewish teachings and culture.
Non-Jewish allies will have an opportunity to learn more about the Jewish culture and people and will be invited to engage in enriching experiences by taking part in our traditions with us. We are also a space for people who are interested in converting to Judaism.
In addition all students who attend meetings will get to enjoy different Jewish foods such as challah and bagels.

Mission
The mission of the CSU Project Rebound Consortium is to support the higher education and
successful reintegration of the formerly incarcerated through the mentorship and living
example of other formerly incarcerated students, graduates, faculty, and staff. Project Rebound
constructs a life-affirming alternative to the revolving door policies of mass incarceration by
making higher education more accessible and supportive of formerly incarcerated students so
that they can acquire the knowledge and skills of a university education, enhance their
capacity for civic engagement and community leadership, secure meaningful and gratifying
employment, empower themselves and their families, and ultimately make stronger, safer
communities.
Vision
We envision a just and equitable work in which all people, including those with an incarceration experience, have access to high-quality higher education and comprehensive student support services that foster achievement, transformation, empowerment, social responsibility and flourishing.
Guiding Values:
The Intrinsic Value of Persons. We believe that every person has inherent value and holds the power of possibility and transformation within them.
Equitable Access to Education. We believe that access to meaningful, high-quality, face-to-face higher education is fundamental to breaking intergenerational cycles of poverty, abuse, addiction, unemployment, and confinement.
Formerly Incarcerated Leadership. We believe that the integration, education, and leadership of formerly incarcerated people are essential to the work of creating solutions to the social crisis of mass incarceration.
Education as Public Safety. We believe that meaningful, high-quality higher education ultimately makes stronger, safer communities; we believe that public resources are better invested in education and other opportunities for transformation than prisons and punishment.
Civic Engagement. We believe that community engagement is at once a right, a responsibility, and a means of empowerment; we aim to inspire all Rebound Scholars to be informed and engaged civic agents.

CSU Monterey Bay’s Project Rebound program supports the success of formerly incarcerated individuals as they work to transform their lives through higher education. This transformative program supports individuals in achieving their educational goals, offering a second chance at success. . We offer special admissions for those who might not normally qualify for university acceptance due to application deadlines, minor academic deficiencies, and other related barriers. Project Rebound recognizes the importance of access to quality education for all and assists motivated individuals to prepare, apply, enroll, and graduate with a university degree.
Project Rebound staff serve as liaisons with campus services and programs, as well as with community organizations. By offering resources and connections with supportive entities, we assist students with meeting their basic needs so they can concentrate on gaining experience in their field of study and achieve educational and personal empowerment.

Theta Alpha Sigma is a Catholic based service and social sorority, which is founded on the premise of the following Six Core Elements: Sisterhood, Academic Support, Emotional Support, Community Service, School Participation, Spiritual Growth. FAQ
● How much can I request, what is a Club Cap?
○ A club can request $1200 from the ICC every Academic School year
○ Additionally, once a club has used their $1200, they can request another $1200
through the ICC General Fund that needs to be approved by the General
Council.
● How can I see how much ICC funds my club has remaining?
○ Email icc@csumb.edu
● How do I check my club's trust account?
○ Email icc@csumb.edu
● How quickly will I get the items I ordered?
○ Order at least 3 weeks in advance to get the items on time. Things can always go
wrong so the earlier you submit a proposal, the better.
● What should my presentation look like?
○ It should look exactly like this: ICC Funding Proposal (ClubName) 2025/2026
● When are the executive/general council meetings?
○ General council meetings are the first Monday of every month from 12pm-2pm in
OSU rm 210.
○ Executive council meetings are every Monday other than the first Monday of the
month from 12pm-2pm in the OSU, rm 311.
● What if I can’t make it to the executive/general council meeting?
○ You can either attend a later meeting for your funding proposal or send someone
else from your club to present for the proposal.
● When should I submit my proposal?
○ Proposals can be submitted at any time, but the deadline to be seen at Monday’s
council is always Friday at 8am.
○ In order to be seen as fast as possible proposals should be submitted before this
deadline.
● Can I purchase food?

How to Start an ICC-Recognized Student Organization
When can I start a new organization?
New groups can only register in the months of November and April to start the following
semester. i.e., November registration means the organization will not be active till the start of
the spring semester. April registration means the organization will not be active till the start of
the fall semester.
What is ICC?
If it’s not a sports club or a social greek organization, then it’s an Inter-Club Council (ICC)
Organization. ICC is the governing board for all Inter-Club Council Organizations. There is an
elected executive board that is made up of a Chair, Treasurer, Secretary, and Public Relations
Officer. The board leads the weekly funding request meetings and the monthly all-council
meetings (every RSO is required to have a representative present at the monthly meetings).
What are the benefits of being a Recognized Student Organization (RSO)?
● Free room reservations for your meetings and events
● Publicity via MyRaft, and some may be featured in the weekly email newsletter: Otter Be
Involved.
● An RSO Financial account is set up and maintained for you by SELD
● Access to the tier system
● Access to request student fee money for RSO programming
● Training is vital for the success of your organization
● Otter Showcase tabling opportunity in order to recruit new members.
● And more
Where do I register a student organization?
On MyRaft.
You can get to MyRaft from your dashboard or by going to myraft.csumb.edu. Sign in with your
CSUMB credentials. Once you log in, click on the group’s tab at the top of the page. Then you
will see a blue box that says register new ICC group, click on it and fill out the form.
Important to note that the form is open year-round, but organizations will only be reviewed and
approved in the months of November and April.

For Event Organizers
(Updated as of February 2026)
UACE ROLE:
University Affairs, Ceremonies, and Events (UACE) serves as the special events
department for campus and community events. UACE educates, facilitates, and
communicates to ensure all campus sponsored events (either on or off campus
grounds) are held safely and successfully, within the established guidelines and
protocols. UACE manages several event facilities on campus. In those managed
facilities, we offer full-service event support. This includes having an event specialist
assigned to your event. In non-managed spaces on campus, UACE offers limited support
services which includes providing expert event advice, direction and training on
submitting service requests as well as submitting a catering request. We also interface
with Catering to ensure food and beverage, if ordered, is delivered and set up in the
correct location. The UACE Administrative Support Event Coordinator is the primary
point of contact for non-managed spaces. They are available by calling (831) 582-4001
or via email at specialevents@csumb.edu.
The information below is provided to give you a broad overview of critical information
needed to book and host an event. Please read these protocols thoroughly. You are
required to acknowledge you have read and understand them when requesting a space.
UNIQUE EVENT NAME:
Please select and use a unique name for each event prior to submitting your request in
25Live. Once submitted into 25Live, event names changes are not allowed. You must
also use the same event name for all other campus services associated with your event
(including, but not limited to, Catering, FMD, Parking Services, etc.). Selecting and
using a unique name for each event is critical to ensure your event receives the
resources it needs to be held safely and successfully. Thank you.
EVENT STAFFING
Event professionals are required for all events held in UACE managed facilities. Outside
of regular business hours, there may be a charge for staffing. The following staffing
schedule is used by UACE to determine appropriate event staffing levels. However,
please check with your event professional for specifics:
0 - 50 guests 1 UACE staff member
51- 150 guests 2 UACE staff members
150 - 250 guests 3 UACE staff members
250+ guests 4+ UACE staff members
Please note, UACE staffing's primary responsibility is safety and logistics. They do not
staff check-in desks, meet and greet attendees, operate audio visual equipment or
handle other administrative tasks. UACE staff is in addition to any staffing provided by
your department/organization to handle these types of tasks.
BILLING/PAYMENTS:
Campus clients: For internal groups, a complete chartstring (which includes all four
components: the unit, account, fund, and department) as well as the executed estimate
(signed by the department authorized signer) must be returned a minimum of 14 days
prior to the event date or the event is subject to cancellation.
Community clients: A signed estimate and contract, a credit card guarantee, a 50%
deposit and proof of insurance are required to be completed not later than 30 days prior
to the event date.
Estimates are good for 30 days. Events submitted after the booking period (14 days in
advance for campus clients and 30 days in advance for community clients) will not be
processed without a chartstring or credit card guarantee.

● The information gathered during pre-registration is to be used for check-in at

Events Pre-Event Checklist and incorporate sustainability into all events.

This policy establishes systemwide policies, procedures, and guidelines for student organizations and
activities. All provisions in this policy are expected to be implemented by the 2023-2024 academic year.
Campuses are authorized to set earlier implementation time lines for any of the provisions.
Student Organizations
Student organizations comprise a vital part of the college student experience and can contribute to
student success and engagement. Participation in student organizations affords students the
opportunity to develop organizational and leadership skills, foster capacities for effective teamwork, and
promote civic engagement and community service, while connecting with peers, faculty and staff.
A campus' recognition of a student organization in accordance with the policy or administration of funds
generated by the student organization does not express or signify that the campus approves or endorses
the organization's goals, activities, or points of view, or that the campus supervises or otherwise controls
the student organization or its activities. Nevertheless, and provided that a student organization meets
and maintains campus requirements for recognition, campuses provide to student organizations certain
benefits and privileges (e.g., use of designated on-campus facilities free of charge, funding
opportunities, support for on-campus program planning, and information regarding basic event
management and financial management practices).
Campuses shall establish and publish procedures for formal chartering and recognition of student
organizations in compliance with the following policies:

assistant salaries, insurance, facility rental fees, equipment rental fees, facility charges
(cleaning, audio-visual, etc), materials, uniforms/costumes/clothing, public performance fees
(for movies/films), dues/membership fees (national organizations), technology (web hosting),
travel and transportation, parking, conference registration fees, event admission fees,
decorations, and publicity/advertising.
Section 1.2 - Procedure:
Potential unauthorized activities and/or expenses will be considered by the Advisory Council where an initial inquiry
of the existence and severity of the potential infraction will be made.
1. A cease and desist letter may be given to the club/organization or individual club/organization affiliates
to allow for a thorough inquiry.
2. Inquiry of alleged UAE infractions may include additional investigation by the Conduct Officer, Dean of
Students, and/or Title IX and Discrimination, Harassment, and Retaliation.
3. Following investigation, the club will be given their due sanction.
4. Upon completion of sanction and period of inactivity, club/organization may reactivate to gain active
status.
5. Failure to deliver on an assigned action plan may result in higher level sanctioning.
Section 1.3 - Sanctions:
Sanctions are determined on three levels - Low, Medium and Severe - for any student organization that engages in
unauthorized activities and/or expenses.
Levels of Severity
1. Low level sanctions for UAE infractions may include, but are not limited to:
a. Club/organization meets with the council advisor
b. Create action plan for club to ensure infraction does not happen again
c. Club/organization maintains active standing pending decision of the council advisor
2. Medium level sanctions for UAE infractions may include, but are not limited to:
a. Club/organization will be suspended for a definite amount of time (i.e. one semester, one
academic year)
3. Severe level sanctions for UAE infractions may include, but are not limited to:
a. Club/organization will be suspended for a definite amount of time (i.e. one semester, one
academic year), or club may be entirely deactivated

What are sports clubs:
The Sport Clubs Council supports student-led sports organizations that promote health, competition, and team building. These clubs offer opportunities for students to play sports recreationally or competitively while building community and school pride.
Types of sports clubs include:
Competitive Teams – Represent CSUMB in club competitions (e.g., Men’s Soccer Club, Women's Rugby Club)
Recreational Clubs – Encourage active lifestyles and wellness (e.g., Surf Club, Hiking Club)
Clubs are open to all skill levels and usually involve regular practices, events, and tournaments.
How to get started:
To be recognized as a CSUMB student club or organization, you will go through a simple recognition process that helps ensure groups are aware of their responsibilities and privileges. This allows each group to operate as independently as it desires and receive as much assistance as it needs.
This registration process occurs during November and April (once per semester)! Please reach out to our SCC email to have us help you begin the process.

Student Engagement and Leadership Development
In this section
Student-Led Leadership, Advocacy and Support for Campus Life
Associated Students (AS) is the official student government organization at Cal State Monterey Bay. Associated Students represents your voice in campus decision-making and oversees programs, services and funding that support campus life.
Through collaboration with university administration and campus departments, Associated Students helps address concerns, allocate resources and guide initiatives that shape your experience. This includes support for campus events, student organizations, sports clubs, media and services used throughout the year.
Associated Students also offers ways for you to take part in leadership, advocacy and campus operations. Through elected positions, councils, committees and paid roles, you can gain experience while contributing to the campus community.
Our Purpose
Mission
Associated Students exists to represent your voice, support your involvement, and create opportunities that help you feel connected, supported, and engaged on campus.
Vision
Associated Students envisions a campus where you have real opportunities to lead, collaborate, and help shape decisions that affect your experience and the wider university community.
Values
The work of Associated Students is guided by equity, advocacy, collaboration, transparency and a commitment to creating inclusive spaces where you feel welcome and heard.

Frequently Asked Questions
What does Associated Students support on campus?
Associated Students supports clubs, organizations and student-led initiatives across campus. Through funding, advising and coordination, Associated Students helps groups plan events, manage budgets and stay connected to campus resources.
General student organizations are supported by the Inter Club Council (ICC), while sports and recreation teams are supported by the Sports Club Council (SCC).
What services can I use through Associated Students?
You can access a variety of services through Associated Students, including discounted tickets to local attractions and events, support for campus programming and other student-focused resources that change throughout the year.
Availability may vary by semester, so stopping by the Associated Students office is the best way to learn what’s currently offered.

What is Otter Media and how do I participate?
Otter Media is a student-run media organization supported by Associated Students. It offers opportunities in broadcasting, live production, music and creative storytelling.
You don’t need prior experience to get involved. Whether you want to be on air, behind the scenes or exploring creative media, Otter Media offers hands-on opportunities to learn and collaborate.
For more information, email

.
What do I need to know to run for office in Associated Students?
Associated Students holds elections every spring semester. Elections give you the opportunity to run for a paid leadership position and represent student voices in campus decision making.
Positions include executive roles and other leadership opportunities within Associated Students. Campaign materials, rules, timelines and eligibility requirements are provided each election cycle.
If you’re considering running, it’s important to review the official elections packet, code of elections and Associated Students bylaws. These documents outline deadlines, campaign guidelines and expectations for candidates.
All election materials must be submitted by the stated deadlines, either in person or by email, as instructed during the election period. Missing deadlines or violating guidelines may result in disqualification.
Questions about Associated Students elections can be directed to the Associated Students Elections Commissioner. You can reach the elections team at
aselections@csumb.edu
for guidance, clarification or support during the process.
